chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I perform ghusl from janābah, and the water falls upon the hard stone surface, then splashes up and falls upon the garment. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is not permissible to separate the acts of wudu; up to his statement: if he breaks up his wudu due to necessity until what had preceded of it dries, he must restart the wudu from its beginning; and if it has not dried, he may continue it from where he stopped.

That which indicates this is His, the Exalted’s, saying: “O you who believe! When you rise for salat, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles.”

And it has been established with us that a command requires immediacy, and delay in it is not permitted. So when that is established, and the one commanded with salat is commanded with wudu before it, then it is obligatory upon him to perform the wudu immediately after the command is directed to him; and likewise all four limbs, because when he has washed his face, he is then commanded after that to wash the two hands, so it is not permissible for him to delay it. And this is also from the perspective of the sunnah.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment onto which the splashed water falls
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer for which wudu is required
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the ankles, mentioned in the verse of wudu
key_terms.الْمَرَافِقِ: the elbows, the limit for washing the hands in wudu
key_terms.لِضَرُورَةٍ: due to necessity, which may excuse an interruption
key_terms.يَجِفَّ: to dry, the condition affecting whether wudu must be restarted

ai.seo_question: Does splashed water during ghusl affect clothing, and must wudu be performed continuously without long interruption?
ai.summary: This passage contains a report from Imam Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that water splashing back onto a garment during ghusl from janābah causes no problem. It then presents al-Shaykh’s legal discussion that continuity in wudu is required, and that if interruption causes the previous moisture to dry, the wudu must be restarted, supported by the Qur’anic command regarding purification before salat.
